desc: Prove/verify the reduction: Manhattan = arc is FALSE in general (counterexample (8,0),(1,10), side=10), but rescued by k ≥ 4: answer ≤ P/k ≤ side, and for D ≤ side, Manhattan ≥ D ⟺ arc ≥ D (same/adjacent edges: equal; opposite edges: Manhattan ≥ side ≥ D). Reduction valid.
Implement perimeter mapping: bottom t=x; right t=side+y; top t=2*side+(side−x); left t=3*side+(side−y); sort by t. (Verified corner consistency, no duplicates.)

Design feasibility check can(D): greedy earliest-pick on ring from each start; wrap constraint last ≤ first + P − D. O(n²) too slow → use two-pointer nxt array + binary lifting (k−1 ≤ 24 jumps, ≤5 levels) for O(n log k) per check.
Binary search bounds: lo = 1 (distinct integer points ⇒ D=1 always feasible), hi = P//k ≤ side (proven upper bound; must NOT exceed side or arc-check becomes invalid for opposite-edge pairs).

Implement the full solution with type hints, test against the three examples plus edge cases (k = n, points clustered on one edge, side = 1, large side), and verify complexity (~31 × O(n log k) ≈ few million ops).
